scope: Corollary 6.5 (Coarse bounds and quiet profiles) of the manuscript “Rigidity of Smooth Billiards with a Continuous Caustic Collar” (preprints/Rigidity-of-Smooth-Billiards-with-a-Continuous-Caustic-Collar-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 147 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0fefc18481d52acb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 63-64. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let dn → 0, bn ≥ 1, and xn ∈ R. Suppose, on a sufficiently large fixed cone starting at depth dn, that dn bn M(s) ≤ C(dn/δs)α , 1 2 < α < 1. (6.19) The following statements hold; whenever an arbitrary fixed aperture is used, the hypothesis is required on its corresponding fixed enlargement. (i) On a strictly coarser cone, starting at a fixed sufficiently large multiple of dn, there is a passage with parameter radius c(dn/bn)(δ/dn)α, and |s − y| = O  b2 n|t|2 d2α−2 n δ1−2α  . (6.20) Equivalently, for Y = (y − xn − iH)/dn, S = (s − xn − iH)/dn, and T = tbn/dn, |S − Y | ≤ C|T|2 (−ℑY )1−2α far enough down at each bounded T. (ii) Suppose in addition that dn bn M(xn + iH + dnS) −→ 0 (6.21) uniformly on every compact subset of ℑS < 0. For every c1, T1 > 0, lift passages reach depth c1dn for all |t| ≤ T1dn/bn, for large n. At real parameters, with ∆(t) = H − hX(t), sup |T|≤T1 ∆(Tdn/bn) dn −→ 0. (6.22) 63 (iii) The hypotheses in (ii) are impossible if bn stays bounded. In fact a vanishing weighted cone bound down to a sufficiently small fixed positive depth ratio already gives this contradiction.
